entities.summary:
Donnchad mac Domnaill Remair, also known as Donnchadh mac Domhnall Reamhair, was a late-eleventh-century ruler of the kingdoms of Leinster and Dublin. He was a son of Domnall Remar mac Máel na mBó.

Born around 1030, Donnchad ascended to the throne of Leinster and Dublin after the death of his father in 1049. His reign was marked by power struggles with his brother, Máel na mBó, and the Viking-ruled Dublin.

In 1070, Donnchad led a military campaign against the Vikings, capturing key strongholds and expanding Dublin's influence.

Despite his military successes, Donnchad's reign was cut short when he was slain in 1089 by a group of rival claimants led by his brother.

Donnchad's legacy as a military leader and politician has endured, with his successors continuing to rule the kingdoms of Leinster and Dublin.

His reign also saw the rise of the Church in Dublin, with the establishment of the Dublin Cathedral.

The 12th-century historian, Henry II of Ireland, wrote: 'Donnchadh mac Domhnall Reamhair was a great king, who ruled over the kingdoms of Leinster and Dublin, and his memory is still revered today.'

Today, Donnchad mac Domnaill Remair is remembered as a pivotal figure in Irish history, whose military campaigns and political savvy helped shape the course of Dublin's development.
